title: Sundown cohort orchestration playbook (notes)
content:
Quick context: experimental small-batch rollout for 'sundown' (RC-2026-02). Personal scratchpad for sequencing cohorts, warmup heuristics, and safety checks. Not a final runbook — capture of my run-through and open questions.

Goals:
- Validate that RC-2026-02 has no perf regressions at 95th latency and P50 under standard traffic shapes.
- Expose model-output regressions on our core prompt suite (search/summary/assist) with synthetic and live traffic.
- Keep customer-visible impact < 0.2% error/failure and <1% quality regressions during canary.

Scope and constraints:
- Hosted API + dedicated fallback. Traffic steering via route flag 'sundown.enabled' and per-tenant pinning.
- Start in region us-west1, expand to eu-central after green.
- Use pre-warmed pool of instances (min-ready: 20 pods) to reduce cold starts.

Cohort definitions (rough):
- Cohort A (shadow-only): 1% sampled traffic, no client-visible changes, just shadow infer + scoring. 24h.
- Cohort B (soft-canary): 0.5% live traffic, percent-of-requests routed to RC for half of session (session sticky). 12h baseline.
- Cohort C (anchor): 5% live traffic, <= 2 tenants with higher SLA pinned; monitor for anomalies. 48h observation.
- Ramp windows: only during 08:00-20:00 local business hours; avoid midnight spikes.

Warmup checklist (before each cohort):
- Deploy RC to dedicated pool, confirm kernel selection logs (xla/opt flags) match expected.
- Fire 50 warmup prompts of each type (short/long/chat/stream) to populate KV cache.
- Verify host metrics: memory stable, GPU util < 70% steady during warmup.
- Verify readiness probes pass for 10 consecutive checks.

Canary exit criteria (must pass all):
- Request error rate delta (RC vs baseline) < 0.2% (5 minute rolling).
- 95th latency delta < +30% and absolute < 700ms for long prompts; P50 delta < +15%.
- A/B eval on guarded prompt set: no more than 0.8% drop in quality score (weighted across tasks).
- No increase in client-side retries or 5xx trends in linked services (auth, routing).

Immediate rollback triggers (auto/ops manual):
- Sustained error delta > 0.5% for 10m.
- QoS regression on production prompt suite > 1.5% after 30m.
- Unexpected spike in token billing (cost-per-token > 20% difference) with no explainable traffic shift.

Observability queries I use (copy-paste later):
- requests: rate(requests_total{route="/generate",model="RC-2026-02"}[5m])
- latency P95: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_bucket{model="RC-2026-02"}[5m])) by (le))
- error ratio: sum(rate(requests_total{status=~"5..",model="RC-2026-02"}[5m])) / sum(rate(requests_total{model="RC-2026-02"}[5m]))
- quality regression probe (simple): POST to eval harness comparing RC vs baseline on prompt-set v3.

Operational notes / tactics:
- Use tenant affinity to avoid flipping high-risk enterprise tenants during B->C ramps. Pin those to baseline until final signoff.
- If we see soft regressions in hallucination measures, throttle to shadow mode and run focused evals against failure cases.
- Keep a 'quiet window' rollback script ready: one CLI that flips route flags and scales down RC pool. Test it in staging.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide warmup prompt anonymity: do we use sanitized real prompts or synthetic copies? (Maya: preference for sanitized real traffic replay).
- Who owns client communication for tenants affected in Cohort C? Tagging product/CS.
- Add synthetic load generator to hit mixed-length tails more aggressively (Cole to prototype).

Post-deploy: brief template
- Timestamp + cohort moved to X%.
- Key metrics snapshot (QPS, P50/P95, error rate, billing delta).
- Notes on unexpected behaviors and actions taken.
- Owner signoff: Rahul, Maya, SRE on duty.

Personal shorthand: if green after Cohort C (48h) -> prepare staged global flip with staggered region ramps (us-east -> eu-central -> apac). If any step fails, immediate pinback to baseline and create postmortem draft within 24h.

Scratch-end: remind self to save final checklist into Confluence (CONFLUENCE-4298) and link the rollout dashboard snapshot.

-- Rahul
